propositions: The live external test guard at test_provider_matrix_live.py:88 fails because it performs literal string comparisons of resolved model specs against REBAR_EXPECTED_LLM_PROVIDER, but the resolver now canonicalizes openai specs to 'openai-chat:' qualifier while the expected value is 'openai' family name.

The _live_llm.py credential map has no 'openai-chat' entry, so configured_provider() returns 'openai-chat', credential_present() fails, live_llm_ready() becomes False, and all live LLM tests on the openai arm silently skip with 'credential absent'.

Commit 8f4c5fdb0d3 updated the unit-tier matrix gate with _MODEL_QUALIFIER_BY_PROVIDER mapping but failed to update the live external tier's consumers (test assertions and credential lookup), creating an unmet consumer obligation.

The guard's intent (verify the arm runs its declared provider family) remains valid; the failure is a false positive because openai-chat and openai name the same provider family per the introducing commit's semantics.

The fix adds a qualifier-to-family mapping (_PROVIDER_FAMILY_BY_QUALIFIER) in _live_llm.py and a provider_family() helper so configured_provider() returns the family name, aligning credential lookup, live_llm_ready(), and guard assertions with the declared arm provider.
The fix does not change the resolver's openai-chat canonicalization (contract side); the guard retains its teeth to catch genuinely wrong providers (e.g., anthropic specs on the openai arm).
